title: Fal AI MCP Server: Connect Claude, ChatGPT & Agents
summary: Fal AI MCP servers let AI agents use fal.ai's image, video and audio models as tools. You can connect them to your agent infrastructure.
body_markdown:
## Connecting fal to your agent in two stages


Because those details drift, the order matters. First create a key and prove one generation works without any agent. Then add the server entry to your client and confirm its tools appear.


### Create a fal API key and test it


Create a fal account, generate an API key from the dashboard's keys page, and export it as` FAL_KEY` in the shell you'll test from. Then call one model directly, with fal's client or a plain HTTP request copied from the model's own page.


If that returns an image or a clip, the account, key and billing all work. If it fails, you have a credentials problem, and it would otherwise surface later as a vague tool error inside the agent.


Keep the key out of any file you commit.


### Local server versus hosted remote endpoint


If your client launches the server as a process on your machine, that is a local server: it needs a runtime installed and reads` FAL_KEY` from its environment.


A hosted remote endpoint is a URL your client connects to, so nothing is installed, but your key travels in a request header and you depend on someone else's uptime.


Choose local when you want the key to stay on your machine. Choose remote when several people or devices share one setup. Take the package name or URL from fal's current documentation, not from a blog post, this one included.


### Configure the fal MCP server in your client


In Claude Desktop, Cursor and most other clients, you edit a JSON file with a server map. A local entry has three fields that matter:` command` , the executable that starts the server;` args` , the arguments passed to it; and` env` , where` FAL_KEY` goes.


A remote entry replaces these with a` url` plus whatever auth header fal specifies.


Restart the client after saving, because most only read the file at launch. A trailing comma or a wrong path usually shows up as a server that silently never appears.


### Confirm the tools and run a real prompt


Open the client's tools list and read it before you prompt anything. Every tool listed is something the agent may call, and each call can bill your account.


**315 items are selected for project users** in the admin dialog below, which comes from an automation platform. A list that long is one nobody reviewed line by line, which is where an agent's tool set drifts if you never prune it.


Disable anything you wouldn't hand over deliberately. Then run one small prompt, such as a single low-resolution image from a cheap model, and check the result against your fal usage page. That tells you the whole chain works and what one call actually costs.
